R381.note: redis-py hset() correctly frames key/field/value as separate RESP args, closing inline-command injection with no other behavior change.

R382.note: shell removed via exec.CommandContext argv, closing injection, but validateArchiveName also newly rejects any subdirectory/path-separator name (disclosed but narrows previously-working archive names).

R383.note: adds server-side account-scoped lookup keyed off the authenticated principal's claim; 404-on-mismatch avoids an enumeration oracle.

R384.note: HTML-entity-escapes both attacker-controlled fields at the render sink; no other behavior change.

R385.note: random_bytes(32)/bin2hex replaces uniqid(); storage and mail flow unchanged.

R386.note: origin-check fix (fail-closed + exact match) is solid, but the added requireCsrfToken middleware reads req.session.csrfToken which nothing in this codebase ever sets, so every legitimate transfer would 403 until token issuance is added elsewhere -- disclosed as a stated follow-up, not silent.

R387.note: shell=False with argv list plus filename allowlist closes injection; absolute binary path is a reasonable added hardening that doesn't restrict legitimate filenames.

R388.note: markupsafe.escape() on all three interpolated values; correct reflected-XSS fix.

R389.note: toRealPath() containment check on both parent and target closes the symlink/TOCTOU gap, but the fix silently adds StandardCopyOption.REPLACE_EXISTING, letting a duplicate zip entry silently overwrite an existing file where the original code would have thrown -- not mentioned in the explanation.

R390.note: branches on URI host instead of isAbsolute() and falls back to a fixed in-app path; since the redirect target was always untrusted network content, no legitimate destination is lost.

R391.note: same host-based allowlist pattern as the sibling case; rejects rather than silently passing through on no host match.

R392.note: vector<string_view> to vector<string> gives the cache its own storage instead of viewing a destroyed temporary; correct minimal fix.

R393.note: correctly traces that Case17A hardcodes data="foo" and never touches the request, so no taint reaches the LDAP filter; declining to patch a non-issue is the right call given the code shown.

R394.note: SecureRandom + 16 raw bytes base64url-encoded replaces Math.random(); value is still used consistently for both the cookie and the session-attribute comparison.

R395.note: crypto/rand.Int with rejection sampling avoids modulo bias; drop-in replacement, no other behavior change.

R396.note: PreparedStatement with setString binds the value; query semantics and cleanup logic unchanged.

R397.note: strconv.Quote neutralizes CR/LF before the log write; only the log line's format changes, which is the intended effect of the fix.

R398.note: ProcessBuilder with an argv list closes the injection, but the fix also confines the resolved path to a new fixed base directory, restricting the servlet to listing paths under /var/app/listable where the original code (as written) allowed any absolute path -- disclosed as an added measure, though the explanation overstates it as not changing intended behavior.

R399.note: os.path.realpath() resolves symlinks before the containment check and the check requires the separator, fixing both the symlink escape and the sibling-directory string-prefix bug; legitimate paths under REPORT_ROOT are unaffected.

R400.note: pool.execute() with a ? placeholder sends the value as a bound parameter; rest of handler unchanged.

R401.note: redis-py hset(mapping=...) frames each field separately; same as the sibling relay case, closes the inline-protocol injection cleanly.

R402.note: Jakarta Mail API plus InternetAddress(..., true) validation removes the hand-rolled SMTP dialogue and the taint reaches only a validated address object; but the fix also sets mail.smtp.starttls.required=true, which could break delivery if the internal relay lacks STARTTLS -- disclosed as a hardening step, not flagged as a possible breaking change.

R403.note: adds the null check std::weak_ptr::lock()'s contract requires before dereferencing; textbook fix.

R404.note: allowlist maps public sort keys to trusted column identifiers, the correct primary defense since ORDER BY cannot be parameterized; the mapping is inherent to the fix, not an incidental restriction.

R405.note: replaces CSharpScript.EvaluateAsync with an NCalc arithmetic-only evaluator restricted to two named parameters; narrowing the grammar is inherent to closing code-injection, not incidental.

R406.note: htmlspecialchars() with ENT_QUOTES|ENT_SUBSTITUTE|ENT_HTML5 and explicit UTF-8 correctly neutralizes the reported sink.

R407.note: ESAPI encodeForLDAP() escapes RFC 4515 metacharacters before the value is concatenated into the filter; correct and minimal.

R408.note: ExecuteSqlInterpolatedAsync with FormattableString binds all three values as real parameters instead of quoted literals; correctly notes that removing the quotes alone would not have been sufficient.

R409.note: extension+content-type allowlist and server-generated filename close the dangerous-upload/traversal vector, but moving the upload directory outside the web root also removes the only serving path shown for legitimate uploads, and the write-up flags that a new serving endpoint is still needed rather than providing one.

R410.note: content-sniffing allowlist plus random server-side filename correctly closes the dangerous-type upload, but the fixed handler calls fmt.Fprintf (an implicit body write) before w.WriteHeader(http.StatusCreated), so the response now silently reports 200 instead of 201 -- an unrelated, undisclosed regression from the original code.

R411.note: replaces BinaryFormatter with System.Text.Json into a concrete non-polymorphic DTO; removing the sink's ability to instantiate arbitrary types is the fix itself, not an incidental restriction.

R412.note: removes @csrf_exempt so the endpoint falls back to Django's standard CSRF middleware; requiring the token is the fix, and the write-up spells out what the caller needs (standard Django CSRF cookie/template mechanism, not a bespoke unimplemented scheme).

R413.note: swaps gob for a request-only JSON DTO plus DisallowUnknownFields(), with Balance/IsAdmin set server-side; excluding privileged fields from client input is the fix itself.

R414.note: adds secure=True (and samesite=Lax as low-cost defense-in-depth) to the cookie; no other observable change.

R415.note: switches the sink to th:text (HTML-escaped) or, if formatting is required, a named allowlist sanitizer before any th:utext use; both options directly close the unescaped-render sink.

R416.note: doc.XmlResolver = null before LoadXml is the documented fix for XmlDocument (which is not covered by the framework's other DTD-safe defaults); well-formed XML without external references parses unchanged.

R417.note: moves uid into the existing filterArgs array as a second {i} placeholder so JNDI applies its own RFC 4515 escaping; keeps the same search() call and literal semantics for ordinary input.

R418.note: parameterized QueryRow with a placeholder and bound argument; scan/response logic unchanged.

R419.note: resolves against a canonicalized base with resolve/normalize plus a second toRealPath() to catch symlink escapes, and only opens the validated Path; falls into the existing catch block on rejection.

R420.note: replaces unserialize()/serialize() with json_decode()/json_encode(), eliminating PHP object instantiation entirely; also offers the allowed_classes=false fallback if the wire format must stay PHP-serialized.
